plan.title: Explore dataset structure and statistics
plan.description: Write scratch.py to examine: (1) number of images, annotations, categories, (2) annotation distribution per image (min/max/mean), (3) category frequency distribution (how many categories have <5, <10, <20 annotations), (4) image sizes, (5) bbox size distribution, (6) how many categories have reference images, (7) category 356 'unknown_product' frequency, (8) sample a few annotations to understand the data format thoroughly.
plan.success_criteria: Complete statistical summary of the dataset logged, understanding of class imbalance and data characteristics

plan.title: Explore reference product images and linkage
plan.description: Write scratch.py to: (1) count product folders and image types in data/products/, (2) check how many annotated product_codes have matching reference image folders, (3) examine which categories lack reference images, (4) check image sizes/quality of reference photos, (5) understand the mapping from category_id -> product_code -> reference images.
plan.success_criteria: Clear mapping between annotations, categories, and reference images documented

plan.title: Train YOLOv8 detection-only baseline (all classes mapped to single class)
plan.hypothesis: A YOLOv8m model trained for detection-only (single class) on 248 images can achieve detection_mAP@0.5 > 0.5, giving final_score > 0.35
plan.description: Convert COCO annotations to YOLO format with a single class (all products = class 0). Split data into train/val (e.g., 200/48). Train YOLOv8m with appropriate augmentations for dense shelf detection. Use 640 or 1280 input size. Evaluate detection mAP@0.5 on validation set. Submit predictions with category_id=0 for all detections.

plan.title: Optimize detection model - larger input size and YOLOv8l
plan.hypothesis: Using larger input resolution (1280px) and YOLOv8l will improve detection of small/dense products
plan.description: Train YOLOv8l at 1280px input resolution with detection-only setup. Use mosaic augmentation, appropriate anchor sizes for small objects. Train for more epochs. Compare with step 3 baseline.

plan.title: Train YOLOv8 with full multi-class classification
plan.hypothesis: Training YOLOv8 with all 357 categories directly will add classification mAP on top of detection, improving final_score beyond 0.70 cap
plan.description: Convert COCO annotations to YOLO format with all 357 categories. Train YOLOv8l/x at 1280px. Use appropriate strategies for class imbalance (focal loss is default). Evaluate both detection and classification mAP@0.5.

plan.title: Train with SAHI (Sliced Aided Hyper Inference) approach
plan.hypothesis: Slicing high-res images into overlapping tiles during training and inference will improve detection of small products on dense shelves
plan.description: Implement image slicing: split each 2000x1500 image into overlapping 640x640 or 1024x1024 tiles with corresponding bbox adjustments. Train YOLOv8 on tiles. At inference, run on tiles and merge with NMS/WBF. Compare with full-image approach.

plan.title: Two-stage approach: detect then classify with crop-based classifier
plan.hypothesis: A two-stage approach (strong detector + separate classifier on crops) will outperform end-to-end multi-class detection due to the extreme number of classes
plan.description: Use best detection model from steps 3-6 to get bounding boxes. Train a separate classification model (ResNet50/EfficientNet from timm) on cropped product regions from training data. At inference: detect -> crop -> classify. Evaluate full pipeline.

plan.title: Augment classifier training with reference product images
plan.hypothesis: Adding reference product images (from data/products/) to classifier training will improve classification accuracy, especially for rare classes
plan.description: For each category with reference images, add the reference photos (with augmentations like random background, color jitter, perspective transforms) to the classifier training set. This gives extra training samples for rare classes. Retrain the crop classifier from step 7.

plan.title: Embedding-based retrieval classification using DINOv2/CLIP features
plan.hypothesis: Using pretrained vision features (DINOv2 or CLIP) to match detected crops against reference product images will provide strong classification without per-class training
plan.description: Extract features from all reference product images using a pretrained model (DINOv2 via timm, or torchvision features). Build a reference gallery. At inference, extract features from each detected crop and find nearest neighbor in the gallery. Map to category_id. This is a zero-shot/few-shot approach that leverages reference images.
plan.success_criteria: classification accuracy > 30% on validation crops, meaningful contribution to final_score

plan.title: Fine-tune embedding model on crop-reference pairs
plan.hypothesis: Fine-tuning the embedding model with contrastive loss on (crop, reference) pairs will improve retrieval-based classification significantly
plan.description: Create training pairs: crop from shelf image <-> reference image of same product. Train with contrastive/triplet loss to bring same-product embeddings closer. Use hard negative mining (visually similar but different products). Evaluate retrieval accuracy.

plan.title: Ensemble detection models with Weighted Boxes Fusion
plan.hypothesis: Ensembling multiple detection models (different sizes, resolutions, with/without SAHI) using WBF will improve detection mAP
plan.description: Train 2-3 detection models with different configurations (YOLOv8m@640, YOLOv8l@1280, YOLOv8x@1280). At inference, run all models and merge predictions using ensemble_boxes WBF. Tune WBF parameters (iou_threshold, skip_box_threshold).
plan.success_criteria: detection_mAP@0.5 improvement of >3% over best single model

plan.title: Try RT-DETR for detection
plan.hypothesis: RT-DETR (transformer-based detector available in ultralytics) may handle dense object detection better than YOLOv8 due to attention mechanisms
plan.description: Train RT-DETR-l from ultralytics on the same data setup. Compare detection performance with YOLOv8. If competitive, add to ensemble.
plan.success_criteria: detection_mAP@0.5 competitive with or better than YOLOv8l

plan.title: Optimize inference pipeline for 300s timeout
plan.hypothesis: The full pipeline (detection + classification) can run on all test images within 300 seconds on L4 GPU
plan.description: Profile the inference pipeline. Optimize: (1) batch inference for detection, (2) batch crop classification, (3) consider ONNX export for faster inference, (4) reduce model size if needed. Ensure total inference fits within 300s budget with margin.
plan.success_criteria: Full pipeline runs on 248 images (or estimated test set size) in < 250 seconds

plan.title: Test-time augmentation for detection
plan.hypothesis: TTA (horizontal flip, multi-scale) will improve detection mAP at the cost of inference time
plan.description: Implement TTA for the detection model: run inference at multiple scales and with horizontal flip, merge predictions with WBF. Balance accuracy gain vs. inference time within 300s budget.
plan.success_criteria: detection_mAP@0.5 improvement with pipeline still under 300s

plan.title: Handle unknown_product category strategically
plan.hypothesis: Properly handling category 356 (unknown_product) - either by detecting it or using it as a fallback for low-confidence classifications - will improve final score
plan.description: Analyze unknown_product annotations. Test strategies: (1) classify low-confidence crops as unknown_product, (2) train classifier with unknown_product as explicit class, (3) use embedding distance threshold - if no reference match is close enough, assign unknown_product.
plan.success_criteria: Improved classification mAP from better unknown_product handling

plan.title: Combine best detection ensemble with best classifier
plan.hypothesis: The combination of best detection ensemble + best classification approach will maximize final_score
plan.description: Assemble the final pipeline: best detection model/ensemble from steps 3-6,11-12,14 + best classification from steps 7-10,15. Tune confidence thresholds for both detection and classification. Run full evaluation on validation set.

plan.title: Final submission optimization and packaging
plan.description: Prepare final submission: (1) ensure all model weights fit in 420MB limit (3 files max), (2) verify inference runs within 300s on L4, (3) ensure correct output format, (4) handle edge cases (no detections, corrupted images), (5) verify ultralytics==8.1.0 compatibility, (6) test with restricted imports.
plan.success_criteria: Clean submission that runs within all constraints and achieves best possible final_score
